clauses.reason: Executive Order 11439, signed 1968-12-07 (33 FR 18257), revokes Executive Order No. 11372 of September 18, 1967, which had designated the Lake Ontario Claims Tribunal as a public international organization entitled to the privileges, exemptions and immunities of the International Organizations Immunities Act; the order recites that the Tribunal has discharged its functions and adjourned. The command is a one-time revocation and is performed when the order takes effect. The order has no effective-date wording, so it took effect on signing, 1968-12-07 (the filing date 1968-12-09 and the printing date 1968-12-10 are alternative readings, not ends). The clause is exhausted by performance on that date (owner ruling 2026-10-28: a used one-time command is recorded as exhausted by performance, separate from any surviving consequence; the surviving consequence here is the revoked status of EO 11372, which is not a command of this order). The cited source is the order's own held text, which contains the words hereby revoke. No earlier end is shown in held evidence.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 11439 (33 FR 18257, Federal Register of December 10, 1968; the govinfo PDF text layer), headed Executive Order 11439, Revoking Executive Order No. 11372, signed by Lyndon B. Johnson and dated December 7, 1968 (filed December 9, 1968); number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: the order is one paragraph with one operative command, that Executive Order No. 11372 of September 18, 1967, which designated the Lake Ontario Claims Tribunal as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act, is revoked, made on a recital that the Tribunal has discharged its functions and adjourned. The dossier's single whole-order clause matches. Lifecycle: the command is a one-time revocation performed when the order took effect. The order has no effective-date wording, so it took effect on signing, 1968-12-07; the filing date (1968-12-09) and the printing date (1968-12-10) are alternative readings and are not ends. The clause is therefore exhausted by performance on 1968-12-07. The revoked designation (EO 11372, held text) is a separate instrument and is not a continuing command of this order. Searches: the U.S. Code, eCFR and Office of the Federal Register disposition-note searches record no hit for this order; a held-corpus search for the number 11439 returns only this order's own printings; the order is not in the table of EO 12553 (its held text contains no 11439). No amendment, revocation or supersession of this order is held.

savings.reason: The order contains no savings, exception, effective-date or notwithstanding wording; the held text was read in full. The revocation of EO 11372 was complete on 1968-12-07, so nothing of this order continues; whatever privileges or immunities the Tribunal held under EO 11372 before that date were acts and effects of the revoked order, not commands of this one. Nothing in the held evidence shows a continuing right or duty arising from this order.
